gennady-timchenko.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
gennady-timchenko.summary: US authorities specifically attributed a business relationship with Putin, not merely operation in Russia. That supports a substantial historical patronage inference, while the underlying claims were expressly denied.

support.text: Treasury linked Timchenko’s energy activities to Putin and attributed investments and possible access to Gunvor funds to Putin. These are US government allegations, not a criminal judgment.

counter.text: Reuters reported Timchenko denying that Putin helped build his business and saying contracts were won competitively. Gunvor denied Putin’s involvement.
counter.access: Indexed article passage reviewed; direct retrieval unavailable

counter.text: Gunvor says Timchenko sold his stake in March 2014 and is no longer affiliated with the company. Historical attribution must not imply current ownership.

gennady-timchenko.limitations: The assessment concerns attributed historical relationships. The US announcement does not publish underlying proof of every claim. It does not establish present Gunvor ownership or guilt in a criminal case.

vagit-alekperov.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
vagit-alekperov.period: Lukoil formation and 2010 tax-policy episode; role update in 2022
vagit-alekperov.summary: The reviewed history links government office, privatization leadership and later company-specific policy advocacy. It is stronger than a nationality or sanctions inference, but not proof that every tax concession was improper.
vagit-alekperov.mechanism: Former public office → privatized oil ownership → tax-policy access

support.text: Reuters described Alekperov moving from deputy energy minister to leading Lukoil after organizing its privatization. It also reported Lukoil lobbying for Caspian export-duty relief and Alekperov announcing a government decision.

counter.text: The same report says competing projects already had relief and cites difficult project economics. Equalizing investment incentives is an alternative to personalized patronage.
Alekperov resigned as president and board member in April 2022. A sanctions record retaining an old title is not evidence of his current executive role.

vagit-alekperov.limitations: Historical estimate only. Privatization leadership is not itself proof of asset theft. The source reports an announced tax decision rather than a complete audit of realized benefits. No present executive role is assumed.

leonid-mikhelson.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
leonid-mikhelson.period: Yamal LNG tax proposals and financing, 2010–2016
leonid-mikhelson.summary: Novatek’s Yamal project received identifiable state financing after high-level industrial-policy engagement. This supports a business–state relationship, not automatic proof that Mikhelson bought favoritism.
leonid-mikhelson.mechanism: Strategic gas investment ↔ targeted state support

support.text: Reporting described Mikhelson’s Yamal project and Putin directing ministries to develop tax relief for the region. The 2010 measure was a proposal, not yet a realized award.
Novatek’s financial statements record government approval of 150 billion roubles of National Wealth Fund financing through interest-bearing Yamal LNG bonds.

counter.text: The disclosure describes interest-bearing financing, not a personal gift. The project had other investors; public industrial-development goals are an alternative explanation for support.

leonid-mikhelson.limitations: The estimate covers Mikhelson’s project leadership, not every family member. Financing is not treated as a grant; prospective tax relief is not counted as realized. This is not a finding of bribery or a current sanctions opinion.

michael-bloomberg.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
michael-bloomberg.period: Mayoral and presidential-campaign relationships discussed in 2020
michael-bloomberg.summary: His wealth clearly financed political reach. The reviewed analysis links philanthropy to political support, but shows less about political power generating private commercial returns.
michael-bloomberg.mechanism: Personal wealth and philanthropy → political influence; commercial return unresolved

support.text: Brookings scholar Vanessa Williamson argued that Bloomberg’s philanthropic funding gave leverage over institutions and potential political supporters. This is attributed political analysis, not an adjudicated finding that grants bought endorsements.

counter.text: Bloomberg ended his presidential campaign after failing to secure a path to nomination despite extensive spending. Wealth did not guarantee electoral control.

michael-bloomberg.limitations: This assessment does not equate charitable giving or running for office with corruption. It is limited to political influence discussed in the reviewed record, not a full examination of Bloomberg LP contracts.

warren-buffett.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
warren-buffett.period: Berkshire political spending and federal tax change, 2017–2019
warren-buffett.summary: Berkshire’s regulated businesses have political-access interests, and broad tax policy materially affected its value. The reviewed record does not establish a personalized bargain engineered by Buffett.
warren-buffett.mechanism: Regulated-company access and broad policy gains; personal exchange not established

support.text: At the 2019 meeting, Buffett distinguished his personal politics from Berkshire’s and acknowledged some subsidiaries make political contributions to maintain access comparable to competitors.
support.access: Indexed transcript passage reviewed; direct retrieval unavailable

support.text: Berkshire’s annual report attributed part of its 2017 increase in net worth to the federal tax-law change. This was general legislation, not evidence of a bespoke reward.

counter.text: Buffett said the parent company did not contribute to presidential candidates and stressed that he speaks for himself on politics. Subsidiary political activity is not automatically a personal quid pro quo.
counter.access: Indexed transcript passage reviewed; direct retrieval unavailable

warren-buffett.limitations: Company activity is not automatically Buffett’s personal conduct. General tax gains do not establish favoritism. This is a limited historical review, not a clean bill of health.

bill-gates.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
bill-gates.summary: Research documents considerable influence over global-health priorities. The reviewed philanthropy sources do not establish that this influence replenishes Gates’s personal wealth; influence alone is not enough for our definition.
bill-gates.mechanism: Philanthropic funding → health-policy influence; private-return mechanism unestablished

support.text: Researchers describe the foundation’s donor networks as a means of shaping global-health priorities. This establishes agenda influence, not Gates’s personal financial gain.

counter.text: The foundation says Gates receives neither salary nor profit from its charitable work, and investment returns fund its mission. Its private-company funding carries public-access requirements. This is the foundation’s account, not an independent financial audit.

bill-gates.limitations: A foundation’s mission and legal constraints do not prove absence of all indirect benefit. Neither academic criticism of agenda-setting nor the foundation’s self-description establishes all three dimensions. Microsoft history and personal investments need a separate, broader review before assigning a person-wide score.

steve-ballmer.reviewDepth: Source-led review of the stated episode; not independently reviewed
steve-ballmer.summary: The reviewed civic-data initiative engages lawmakers, but does not demonstrate a preferential commercial benefit to Ballmer. That limited observation is not an assessment of all his business or political relationships.
steve-ballmer.mechanism: Civic information funding → policymaker access; wealth-return link unestablished

support.text: USAFacts identifies Ballmer as its founder and funder and describes briefings, advice and training for Congress. It says it is nonpartisan and offers public access without fees.

counter.text: TIME describes the project as a nonprofit, nonpartisan effort to make government data accessible. The reporting does not establish that the project secures a private business advantage.

steve-ballmer.limitations: USAFacts is not Ballmer’s entire financial or political life. Microsoft-era conduct, sports-arena public policy and other philanthropy require broader review; a civic project cannot be used to infer a low person-wide score.
